text.p: These are the leading stories in Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, sends a letter to U.S. president asking him to intervene in boosting implementation of civilian parts of the Dayton peace accord within the next 14 months after which NATO-led troops are suppose to leave Bosnia.

- I share President Izetbegovic's worries about seccessionists efforts in Bosnia and the gist of the problem lies in the Bosnian Serb leadership but I also think that the President's analysis of the problems should be more convincing, Michael Steiner, deputy High Representative for Bosnia says.

- Bosnian Croat leaders say Izetbegovic's letter of complaints about bad implementation of the peace accord, which was sent to the world's statesmen, should have been first discussed by Bosnia's joint institutions and that the certain evaluations in the letter were biased.

- If those muncipalities in the Moslem-Croat federation which are divided by the inter-entity lines are not formed before the upcoming countrywide local elections, 50,000 people will not be able to vote, officials from the ruling Bosnian Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) say.

- One of the conditions for a meeting between Alija Izetbegovic and Croatian president Franjo Tudjman, planned to take place soon, is forming of the joint Moslem-Croat police in the divided town of Mostar, SDA officials say. - This is a pure use of force with political background in order to justify crimes committed in Srebrenica, Bosnian co-prime minister, Haris Silajdzic, says after three Moslems were sentenced to 20 years of prison by Bosnian Serb court in Zvornik.
